spectral_preprocessing.note: numpy Hann-STFT log band-power -> interp to L; app computes x_spec on the per-window z-scored signal, the graph z-scores both inputs per-window

calibration.evaluation_partition: validation (store_v2) — the same split the temperature grid was minimized on; see held_out_ece for the held-out measurement
calibration.partition_note: the ECE pairs above are measured on the SAME validation split the temperature grid was minimized on, so the post-scaling number is an optimization minimum and optimistic (a held-out replication of the grade head on this graph gave 0.1343 -> 0.1121). held_out_ece below is that replication carried out in full: on 2315 store_v8 test windows from 459 subjects this graph never saw, the grade head's post-scaling ECE is 0.1116 -- 1.71x the 0.0654 above, and within 0.0005 of the 0.1121 quoted here.

held_out_ece.partition: data/store_v8 test split, restricted to subjects absent from both the train and val partitions of data/store_v2 (this graph's training store)
held_out_ece.population_kind: within_distribution: held-out SUBJECTS of all 7 cohorts the model trained on

full_store_v8_test_partition.why_not_the_headline: 30.3% of these windows belong to subjects that were in store_v2's train or val partition -- store.py::_subject_split re-shuffles each cohort's subject list per build, so a store_v8 test subject is not automatically unseen by a store_v2-trained graph

held_out_ece.app_convention_note: the numbers above build x_spec the way the exporter did (on the raw window); the app builds it on the per-window z-scored signal (onnx_runner.py:290-302), which the usable head reads. The grade head reads the raw branch alone and is bit-identical under both (max |dlogit| = 0.0, measured).
held_out_ece.pair_convention: [pre_scaling, as_shipped], same as grade_ece/usable_ece above. The graph emits raw_logits/T, so the pre-scaling logits are recovered exactly as graph_logits * T -- no model was loaded and the baked-in temperature is unchanged.
held_out_ece.estimator: biosqa.xdomain.calibration.expected_calibration_error at its default n_bins=15 (equal-width top-1-confidence bins) -- the same function and bin count that produced grade_ece/usable_ece above, so the two columns are comparable
held_out_ece.measured_by: scripts/measure_heldout_calibration.py (onnxruntime forward over this .onnx; trains nothing, exports nothing)

input_contract.reports: quality of the signal AS PROVIDED — if the input was pre-filtered, this is the post-filter quality
input_contract.caveat: a pre-filtered but still-corrupted signal can be under-flagged (false-clean): an aggressive low-pass/band-limit strips the high-frequency cues the model keys on. The app runs biosqa.inference.prefilter.detect_prefiltering() to warn when the input looks pre-filtered.

ood.coverage_note: this tau was fit on the SUPERSEDED single-branch model and carried over unchanged. Measured on 1390 store_v2 ECG val windows through THIS graph it covers the true grade 88.5% of the time against a nominal 90% (alpha=0.1); a tau re-fit on this graph (0.9830) gives 90.1%. Re-fitting requires a model run, so the value is left as shipped and the measured coverage is stated here instead. The app deliberately surfaces the APS set as ambiguity and never prints a coverage percentage.
